comments.body:
Fix pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1135

Approach as decided: both fallback rules kept, reconciled by a new explicit check at the seam.

- criteria/overlay.py: new check_repo_root_agreement() + RepoRootMismatchError. Discovery's arg is interpreted with discovery's rule (_resolve_repo_root); resolution's is used raw; compared through os.path.realpath. Divergence raises naming BOTH roots, the located 'where', and the remedy. The false symmetry claim in _resolve_repo_root's docstring is corrected.
- prompting/prompts.py: PromptNotFound now distinguishes the three cases (no root supplied -> says project prompts were NOT searched; root supplied -> names the exact absolute path searched; unknown id -> keeps the built-in inventory). get_prompt(repo_root=None) still means packaged prompts only (unchanged resolution behaviour).
- code_review/batch_runner.py: records project_criteria_root and asserts agreement before resolving each rubric; gate_dispatch threads execution_repo_root to both halves.
- plan_review/registry.py: same guard in _descriptor_from_prompt's prompt getter, so plan-review's currently-incidental agreement is enforced. Both gates covered.

RED->GREEN: tests/unit/test_prompt_repo_root_seam.py (15 tests) held out from the implementer. Proven RED first at runtime (the mismatch surfaced as "unknown prompt 'code-review-project-seam'" even though the rubric existed). GREEN after. Mutation-checked twice: restoring the old single not-found message returned 2 tests to RED; deleting both seam checks returned 3 to RED (one plan-review, two code-review).

Full unit suite 6356 passed / 20 skipped; make lint and make typecheck clean.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Criterion DISCOVERY and prompt RESOLUTION resolve their repo root by different rules, and nothing
detects when the two disagree.

- `src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:77-88` (`_resolve_repo_root`) falls back to `config.repo_root()`
  when passed `None`, so a project criterion is ACTIVATED from the ambient checkout.
- `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:213-221` (`get_prompt`) has no fallback: it gates the project
  override lookup on `if repo_root:`, so a `None` root silently skips `.rebar/prompts/` and falls
  through to `PromptNotFound` at :226.

`_resolve_repo_root`'s own docstring asserts it returns "the same root `get_prompt` resolves
`.rebar/prompts/` overrides against". That is FALSE. The symmetry it claims has never existed, so
this is an unenforced invariant, not a deliberate split.

Bug 2ea4 (closed duplicate) was one live instance: criterion activated from cwd, prompt looked up
with `repo_root=None`, hard `LLMError`. Commit `b3953a0da` (ticket 22f5) repaired that one call path
by computing `execution_repo_root = cfg.repo_path` in `llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:698` and passing
it to both stages. Nothing PREVENTS the next caller from reintroducing the split.

Two distinct defects remain:

1. **No detection.** Discovery and resolution take independent `repo_root: str | None` parameters at
   two different depths. A caller can supply different roots, or one and not the other, and the
   mismatch is invisible until it surfaces as an unrelated-looking error.
2. **The error is inaccurate and not remediable.** `PromptNotFound` reports
   `unknown prompt '<id>'; known built-ins: [...]`. For a client project whose `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md`
   exists and is correct, this message is actively misleading: the prompt is not unknown, it was
   never searched for. The message names neither the effective root nor the path that was checked, so
   a client project cannot act on it.

## Decision (made by the operator; do not re-litigate)

Fail loudly, with an accurate error a client project can remediate. Specifically:

- Do NOT give `get_prompt` the ambient `config.repo_root()` fallback. Attested gate runs deliberately
  re-root onto a pinned snapshot (`b3953a0da`); an ambient fallback would load project prompts from the
  developer's working tree while reviewing pinned content and SUCCEED. A silently-wrong review is worse
  than a hard failure.
- Do NOT remove discovery's fallback. That would silently stop activating project criteria for callers
  passing `None` — under-enforcement, quieter and worse than the current loud error.
- Therefore: keep the two fallback rules as they are, and add an explicit check at the seam that the
  root used for discovery is the root used for resolution, failing loudly when they differ.

## Approach

Resolve the root once per run at the entry point and thread one value, rather than resolving it twice
at two depths. Where discovery and resolution meet, verify they agree and raise a descriptive error if
not. Rewrite the not-found error so it distinguishes the three cases and names the remedy:

- a project root WAS supplied and `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` is absent — name the exact path searched;
- NO root was supplied, so project prompts were not searched at all — say so explicitly, rather than
  claiming the id is unknown;
- the id is genuinely not a packaged prompt and no project root could supply it — the current message.

`get_prompt(repo_root=None)` must KEEP meaning "packaged prompts only" and must remain legal: 23 test
call sites and the finalizer at `llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:488` depend on it, and packaged
prompts must resolve with no checkout at all (library use).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py` — the `if repo_root:` guard and the `PromptNotFound` message.
- `src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py` — the seam check; correct the false docstring at :79-81.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py:113-141` — the validation site that surfaces the error.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:259,308,334,519` — aliases `_resolve_repo_root` and calls it at
  three sites, so plan-review shares this seam and must be covered, not just code-review.

## Testing

- A project criterion activated from a root whose `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` EXISTS resolves that prompt
  (client-project override path works end to end).
- A packaged prompt resolves with `repo_root=None` (unchanged; pin the existing contract).
- Discovery root != resolution root raises a descriptive error naming both roots, not `PromptNotFound`.
- A missing project prompt under a supplied root produces a message naming the exact path searched.
- Both gates covered: code-review AND plan-review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Discovery and resolution disagreeing on the repo root fails loudly with an error naming both
      roots; verified by a unit test that supplies mismatched roots.
- [ ] The not-found error distinguishes "no root supplied, project prompts not searched" from
      "root supplied, path absent" and names the searched path; verified by tests on both branches.
- [ ] A client project's `.rebar/prompts/<id>.md` override resolves for an activated project criterion
      in both the code-review and plan-review gates; verified by a test per gate.
- [ ] `get_prompt(repo_root=None)` still resolves packaged prompts; existing 23 test call sites and
      completion_recovery.py:488 keep passing.
- [ ] The false symmetry claim in overlay.py's `_resolve_repo_root` docstring is corrected.
- [ ] make lint, make typecheck, and the default suite exit zero.
compiled_state.title: Prompt resolution and criterion discovery can use different repo roots; the resulting error is inaccurate and not remediable by a client project
